text: dsh-apple-mode（DSH 插件，桌面端）：为 DeepSeek Harness 提供 Apple 平台开发 preset。所选会话通过 mcpbridge 接入 Xcode MCP，提供工作区文件操作与搜索、目标和构建设置管理、诊断、方案切换及本地化工具，并加载 Swift 优先的开发 persona。旧版 DSH 可用安装脚本选择 Xcode、安装磁盘 preset，並从本机 Xcode 生成技能。适合在 DSH 中开发 Swift、SwiftUI 和 Apple 平台项目的用户。需要 macOS、Xcode 26+；使用 MCP 时须打开项目并允许访问。

dsh-apple-mode adds an Apple development preset to DSH. Selected sessions connect to Xcode through mcpbridge for workspace editing, search, settings, and diagnostics, with a Swift-first persona. Legacy DSH can install a disk preset and generate skills locally. Requires macOS and Xcode 26+.
想让 DSH 会话直接操作当前打开的 Xcode 项目。
在 DSH 里用 MCP 搜索和编辑 Xcode 工作区文件。
给 Swift 开发会话加上 Xcode 的项目诊断和构建设置工具。
希望 AI 编程助手按 Apple 平台习惯优先使用 Swift。
怎样让 DSH 查看 Xcode 当前工程的问题并切换运行目标？
I want my DSH coding session to work with the open Xcode project.
Can I use Xcode workspace tools and diagnostics from an MCP-enabled DSH preset?
Help me configure an Apple-focused, Swift-first coding mode in DSH.
dsh-apple-mode 的功能「Xcode 工具」：Apple Mode 会话连接 Xcode MCP，可搜索和编辑工作区并查看诊断；选择 preset 后启动 xcrun mcpbridge。
dsh-apple-mode 的功能「Apple 开发 persona」：为会话设置 Apple 平台优先的工作方式，默认偏好 Swift，并要求先查看项目接口再编写依赖其类型的代码。
dsh-apple-mode 的功能「本地生成技能」：安装器可调用 xcrun agent skills export，将本机 Xcode 提供的技能合并到用户技能目录；技能内容不随仓库分发。
dsh-apple-mode 的功能「选择 Xcode」：旧版安装器检测可用版本，可交互选择或用 --xcode 指定，并将路径写入 preset；也支持运行时选择启动器。通过 install.sh 参数触发。
dsh-apple-mode 使用前须知：Xcode MCP 需要 macOS 上安装 Xcode 26+，并让目标项目在 Xcode 中打开；首次连接需在 Xcode 对话框允许访问。
dsh-apple-mode 使用前须知：Apple 技能由安装器调用本机 xcrun agent skills export 生成并写入用户技能目录；使用技能生成功能需本机具备相应 Xcode。

dsh-apple-mode README · dsh-apple-mode：[English](README.md) · [简体中文](README.zh.md)

**Xcode AI integration mode for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`)** — an agent preset + installer that gives your DSH sessions the full Xcode AI stack:

dsh-apple-mode README · dsh-apple-mode：- **26 Xcode MCP tools** (`mcp__xcode__*`) via Apple's official `mcpbridge`
- **Xcode Intelligence–style persona** (Swift-first, tool-assisted, explain-vs-change classification) adapted from the `IDEIntelligenceChat` prompt templates
- **10 Apple platform skills** (SwiftUI, App Intents, security hardening, bounds safety, …) generated locally from your own Xcode

> 📌 `dsh-plugin` topic repo. DeepSeek Harness is in developer preview — pin an exact `dsh` version for your automation.

dsh-apple-mode README · Why a preset (mode) instead of a global MCP wiring?：The three capabilities map onto three different DSH mechanisms:

| Layer | Capability | DSH mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Execute | 26 `mcp__xcode__*` tools | `dsh-mcp-client` (mounted inside the preset) |
| Knowledge | 10 Apple skills | `dsh-skill-filesystem` (global, lazy-loaded) |
| Behavior | Xcode Intelligence persona | agent preset (this repo) |
section: Why a preset (mode) instead of a global MCP wiring?

text: dsh-apple-mode README · Why a preset (mode) instead of a global MCP wiring?：Wiring the MCP server **globally** would put ~26 large tool schemas (~6k+ tokens/request) into *every* session. Mounting it inside a **preset** keeps the cost only in sessions that opt in — pick **Apple Mode** when creating a session, and you get the whole stack; other sessions stay lean.

text:
dsh-apple-mode README · Requirements：- macOS
- **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.0+** for the plugin path (the desktop app ships 0.2.x). DSH 0.1.x uses the legacy on-disk preset through `install.sh` — see [Version compatibility](#version-compatibility).
- Xcode 26+ (contains `mcpbridge` and `xcrun agent skills export`). To use the MCP tools, Xcode must be **running with the target project open**, and you must click **Allow** on the MCP access dialog Xcode shows (see [Usage](#usage)).

dsh-apple-mode README · DSH 0.2.0+ (desktop app / current) — recommended：Install the plugin with the plugin manager. Its bundle patch declares the **Apple Mode** agent preset:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:jihongboo/dsh-apple-mode"
```

Pin a released version by appending a tag — recommended for reproducibility, since an install without a tag tracks the default branch:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:jihongboo/dsh-apple-mode#v1.1.1"
```

dsh-apple-mode README · DSH 0.2.0+ (desktop app / current) — recommended：(In the desktop app: **Settings → Plugins → install from GitHub**.) Restart DSH, then pick **Apple Mode** when creating a session.

dsh-apple-mode README · DSH 0.2.0+ (desktop app / current) — recommended：> **About the plugin manager's pnpm warning.** This package is configuration-only — no `scripts`, no dependencies, no build step (see `package.json`). If a registry page warns that pnpm ≥ 10 refuses to run git-dependency `prepare` scripts and suggests adding `allowBuilds` to `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, you can safely skip it: there is nothing to build or execute, and granting it would only widen the authorization surface for no benefit. Publishing to npm (see [docs/publishing.md](docs/publishing.md)) removes the warning entirely.

dsh-apple-mode README · DSH 0.2.0+ (desktop app / current) — recommended：Then generate the Apple skills locally — the plugin deliberately does not redistribute them:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/jihongboo/dsh-apple-mode.git
cd dsh-apple-mode
./install.sh --skills-only
```

dsh-apple-mode README · DSH 0.1.x — legacy on-disk preset：```sh
git clone https://github.com/jihongboo/dsh-apple-mode.git
cd dsh-apple-mode
./install.sh
```

`install.sh` then does three things:

1. **Detects your Xcode installs and lets you choose which one provides `mcpbridge`** (see below).
2. Installs the on-disk preset → `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/apple/` (existing copy is backed up).
3. Generates the 10 Xcode AI skills **on your machine** via `xcrun agent skills export` into `~/.agents/skills/`.

dsh-apple-mode README · DSH 0.1.x — legacy on-disk preset：> **Why no vendored skills?** The skills are Apple-authored guidance. Generating them from your own Xcode at install time avoids redistributing Apple content — the repo ships only our own code, config, and docs.

dsh-apple-mode README · Version compatibility：DSH 0.2 renamed and reworked agent presets: a preset is now a `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` **row declared by a bundle patch**, and the registry no longer scans directories.

dsh-apple-mode README · Version compatibility：| DSH | Preset mechanism | How to get Apple Mode here |
|---|---|---|
| **0.2.0+** (desktop) | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` rows from a bundle patch | `dsh plugin --profile web add "github:jihongboo/dsh-apple-mode"` |
| **0.1.x** (older `npx`/brew) | on-disk directories under `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/<id>/` | `./install.sh` |

Skills are discovered from `~/.agents/skills` on **both** versions, so `./install.sh --skills-only` works everywhere.

dsh-apple-mode README · Choosing an Xcode (multiple installs)：If you have several Xcode versions (e.g. `Xcode.app`, `Xcode-beta.app`, `Xcode-26.2.app`), `mcpbridge` lives in each one's `Contents/Developer/usr/bin` — and only in Xcode 26+.

**DSH 0.2.0+:** the preset's MCP row runs `xcrun mcpbridge`, so the Xcode comes from `xcode-select`:

```sh
sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode-26.2.app/Contents/Developer   # switch globally
DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer dsh web  # or per launch
```

dsh-apple-mode README · Choosing an Xcode (multiple installs)：To drive a specific **running** Xcode instance, add `env: { MCP_XCODE_PID: '<pid>' }` to the `mcp-xcode` row inside the preset (edit `cordis.patch.yml` in this repo, or override the `preset-apple` row from your profile patch).

**DSH 0.1.x:** `install.sh` scans `/Applications` for every install that provides `mcpbridge` and prompts you to pick:

dsh-apple-mode README · Choosing an Xcode (multiple installs)：```text
Found Xcode installs providing mcpbridge:
  1) /Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer  (xcode-select default)
  2) /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer
Choose (1-2, default 1):

dsh-apple-mode README · Choosing an Xcode (multiple installs)：- **Default** = the Xcode selected by `xcode-select` → the preset uses `command: xcrun mcpbridge` (portable; follows future `xcode-select` changes).
- **Pick another** → the chosen `…/Contents/Developer/usr/bin/mcpbridge` is baked into the installed preset as an absolute path.
- **Non-interactive**: `./install.sh --xcode /Applications/Xcode.app` (or `--xcode …/Contents/Developer`); `./install.sh --list-xcodes` prints the candidates.
- **Switch at runtime without reinstalling**: `./install.sh --runtime-selectable` installs `bin/mcpbridge` as the command; set `DSH_XCODE_DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/…/Contents/Developer` when launching `dsh` to switch. (Resolution: `DSH_XCODE_DEVELOPER_DIR` → `xcrun` → newest `/Applications/Xcode*.app`.)

dsh-apple-mode README · Choosing an Xcode (multiple installs)：To change the choice later: re-run `./install.sh`, edit the `mcp-xcode` row in `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/apple/agent.cordis.yml`, or use the runtime env var above.

dsh-apple-mode README · Alternative: global MCP wiring (MCP in every session)：The preset keeps the ~26 tool schemas scoped to Apple Mode sessions. To get the Xcode MCP tools in **every** session instead, insert the client row in your profile patch (`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: mcp-xcode
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:

**Use one path, not both**: two live instances with `serverName: xcode` collide and the later one fails to load. See [docs/global-mcp.md](docs/global-mcp.md).
section: Alternative: global MCP wiring (MCP in every session)

text:
dsh-apple-mode README · Usage：1. Restart `dsh` (or just open a **new session** — the preset can only be selected on a blank session).
2. Pick **Apple Mode** as the agent preset when creating the session.
3. The session now has:
   - `mcp__xcode__*` tools — operate the open Xcode workspace: `XcodeRead/Write/Update/MV/RM`, `XcodeGlob/Grep/LS`, `UpdateTargetBuildSetting`/`UpdateFileCompilerFlags`, `XcodeListNavigatorIssues`, scheme/run-destination/test-plan switching, `XcodeNewTarget`, `StringCatalogRead/Edit`, …
   - All Apple platform skills (lazy-loaded on demand).
   - An Apple-first, tool-assisted working style.

dsh-apple-mode README · Usage：> **Before using the `mcp__xcode__*` tools:**
> 1. Xcode must be **running** with the project/workspace you want to work on **opened** in it.
> 2. On first connection, Xcode shows an **MCP access dialog** — click **Allow** (允许). Until you do, tool calls will be rejected.

dsh-apple-mode README · Usage：Build/run/test still happen from the terminal (`xcodebuild`, pipe through [`xcsift`](https://github.com/...) for structured output); the MCP toolset covers project surgery, build settings, diagnostics, destinations, and localization.

dsh-apple-mode README · MCP tools (26, namespaced `mcp__xcode__*`)：| Group | Tools |
|---|---|
| Project I/O | `XcodeRead` `XcodeWrite` `XcodeUpdate` `XcodeMV` `XcodeRM` `XcodeMakeDir` |
| Search | `XcodeGlob` `XcodeGrep` `XcodeLS` |
| Targets & settings | `XcodeNewTarget` `XcodeListTemplates` `XcodeListTargets` `UpdateTargetBuildSetting` `UpdateFileCompilerFlags` |
| Scheme / destination / tests | `XcodeListSchemes` `XcodeSwitchScheme` `XcodeListRunDestinations` `XcodeSwitchRunDestination` `XcodeListTestPlans` `XcodeSwitchTestPlan` |
| Diagnostics | `XcodeListNavigatorIssues` `XcodeRefreshCodeIssuesInFile` |
| Localization | `StringCatalogRead` `StringCatalogEdit` |
| Windows | `XcodeListWindows` `XcodeGetCurrentFile` |

dsh-apple-mode README · Skills (10, generated at install time)：`swiftui-specialist` · `swiftui-whats-new-27` · `app-intents-specialist` · `app-intents-whats-new-27` · `audit-xcode-security-settings` · `adopt-c-bounds-safety` · `uikit-app-modernization` · `modernize-tests` · `device-interaction` · `building-document-based-swiftui-applications`

dsh-apple-mode README · Repository layout：```text
.
├── presets/apple/            # The agent preset: agent.cordis.yml + preset.yml
├── bin/mcpbridge             # Runtime-selectable mcpbridge launcher (--runtime-selectable)
├── cordis.patch.yml          # Bundle patch: declares the Apple Mode preset (DSH 0.2+)

dsh-apple-mode README · Customization：- **Different Xcode:** re-run `./install.sh` (picker), `./install.sh --xcode <path>` (non-interactive), `--runtime-selectable` + `DSH_XCODE_DEVELOPER_DIR`, or add `env: { MCP_XCODE_PID: '<pid>' }` to the `mcp-xcode` row to drive a specific running instance. See [Choosing an Xcode](#choosing-an-xcode-multiple-installs).
- **Persona:** edit the `persona` row text in the same file.
- **Sync skills after Xcode updates:** re-run `./install.sh` (skills are replaced, preset is backed up).
- **Keep in sync with upstream `standard` preset:** `diff` against `node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/config/agent-presets/standard/agent.cordis.yml`.

dsh-apple-mode README · Security notes：- MCP tool calls do **not** go through the DSH file sandbox — they go through the tool-approval flow. `XcodeUpdate`/`XcodeWrite` modify real Xcode project files (including `project.pbxproj`).
- The preset only activates when you select it; no global config is touched by `install.sh`.

dsh-apple-mode README · Contributing：PRs welcome. Open an issue for feature requests. If you publish your own DSH extension, add the [`dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) topic for discoverability and consider submitting it to [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin).
